title: Hightower on rookie class: 'They have a burning desire to achieve greatness' | Press Conference
text: All right, good to see everyone. How's everyone doing? I'm doing outstanding. What you guys got? You got a couple new returners in your unit. So, um two really good options there and um really excited about adding those guys to this roster. You know, I know in the old one, you know, if you actually got the ball, you thought you could take it. But now, pretty good chance you're going to actually return it a lot more. Field position, drive starts, it's changed the way offensive call plays. I mean, matter of a time, you'll be in field goal range. What did he show you when he was with you guys last year? We did we liked him the first time we brought him in in regards to the two snappers. We actually have two guys in the building right now that we're really excited to see when the pads come on. And as your football team gets better the guys that you draft unless they come in and they supersede if they just jump over top of a veteran, they're going to have to play uh special teams. So I like the mindset. I like the mentality uh of those rookies so far. I mean it's early, you know, I could I could tell you that. I mean they're they're dealing with a lot. I mean they're in a new city. Uh they got new faces. Uh they're learning new terminology. Some of them are still in a hotel, you know, but what I can tell you about this group is everything that we were told in the process about these guys, um that is clearly evident. And number one, they're our they're our type of guys. All right, number two, they love football. All right, number three, they can't live without football. Okay, and they're extremely competitive and they have a burning desire to achieve greatness. I like his natural instincts. I like his ability to catch the ball in traffic and his fearlessness. title: Ravens Who Made a Strong First Impression at OTAs |Baltimore Ravens Final Drive
text: The Ravens have wrapped up their first week of OTAs and there have been some early standouts. First round pick Binka Awani has been as advertised. Jessie Minter called him a beast and said the rookie has picked up everything faster than he'd expect at any position. Veteran guard John Simpson called the rookie a sponge and at another spot on the offensive line, center Danny Pinter took reps with the first team and coach Minter said he did a great job. Pinter will continue to rotate through the off-season program with Joe Von Gwenn and Corey Bullock as that competition takes shape during training camp. From an energy standpoint, you can't miss rookie receiver Jacoby Lane on the practice field. You might have seen his backflip, but he was also getting noticed for his play making on the field with offensive coordinator Decklin Doyle taking note. And with some of the veteran corners out, the younger players in the secondary got more reps and Robert Longerbeam who was sidelined for his rookie year with a knee injury took full advantage having an interception and a pass break up. Longerbeam will work to carve out a role in the talented group over the summer. And earlier this week I named safety Malachi Starcs as one of my players to watch during OTAs and the sophomore hasn't disappointed. During this OTA portion, it's a teammate first mentality from a physicality standpoint, but Starcs seems to be in the right spot to make a play often. It was a week of high energy as Jessie Minter establishes his culture as a head coach and for more OTA standouts visit our website. Have a great Memorial Day weekend everyone. We'll be back with you next week.
